subject: Post-demo: Acme model shortlist & recommended next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Joe Turner <joe.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Acme model shortlist & recommended next steps

Hi Sarah / Joe —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and the recommended next steps from our side. I saved the demo recording to the shared folder and attached the initial benchmark pack.

What we heard / priorities:
- High throughput customer-facing summarization and routing (avg. request length ~150 tokens; peak concurrency 90rps)
- Tight latency target for tail p95 <= 350ms for interactive flows
- Budget sensitivity: prefer models that keep inference unit costs lower than $0.008/token for deterministic assists
- Quality is critical on safety/PII redaction and hallucination for compliance workflows

Immediate next steps (proposal):
1) Model shortlist + rationale (attached) — see the table in redwood_model_comparison.xlsx.
2) Shared benchmark report (acme_benchmarks_v1.pdf) with your sample prompts and evals.
3) Technical deep-dive to validate integration & KV cache strategy (Dev + infra).
4) Pilot plan: 2-week A/B with 10k requests/day using canary routing in Dedicated pool.

Attachments included: acme_benchmarks_v1.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.csv, redwood_model_comparison.xlsx

Shortlist summary (high level):
- open-llama-13b-q4: Best cost/latency balance for deterministic summarization; quantized, runs well on our 80GB GPU shapes; recommended if you prioritize throughput over SOTA quality.
- redwood-instruct-7b: Good middle ground — strong safety tuning, lower token cost, p95 latency comfortably under 300ms in our tests, slightly lower recall on long context items.
- gptx-40b-finetune (partner model): Highest quality for hallucination-sensitive tasks; higher cost and p95 ~420ms on equivalent hardware — recommended for a small high-quality routing tier for compliance-critical flows.

Benchmarks and prompt set: I ran the shortlist against your sample prompts (see acme_prompt_set_v1.csv) and included cost/latency/quality tradeoffs in the spreadsheet. The attached PDF highlights where each model failed our hallucination checks and the top 10 problematic prompts.

Please let me know which model(s) you want us to prioritize for a pilot. Rishi and Dev are copied to schedule the technical call.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Acme demo recording: https://redwood.ai/shared/acme-demo-recording

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Joe Turner <joe.turner@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme model shortlist & recommended next steps

Thanks Marissa — great recap and very helpful. Quick notes/questions from our side: 

1) For the pilot, we like the idea of a two-tier approach: primary on open-llama-13b-q4 for most traffic, with gptx-40b-finetune as a fallback for high-risk content. Can you confirm the expected per-token cost delta between those two in your spreadsheet?

2) On safety: a few of our compliance folks flagged the hallucination examples in pages 6-8 of the PDF. Are those reproducible with different seeds/prompts or do they look deterministic to your eval harness?

3) Scheduling: can we do the technical deep-dive this Thursday at 11am PT? Dev and Rishi included?

If that works I can bring our infra lead and procurement on the follow-up.

— Sarah
Senior PM, Product AI | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Joe Turner <joe.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme model shortlist & recommended next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — TBH a two-tier approach is exactly what we recommend for customers with mixed quality/cost priorities. Quick answers inline: 

1) Cost delta: In our spreadsheet (redwood_model_comparison.xlsx) we show per-token inference unit estimates: open-llama-13b-q4 ~ $0.0025/token (quantized, bulk batching assumptions), redwood-instruct-7b ~ $0.004/token, gptx-40b-finetune ~ $0.012/token. These are ballpark and depend on batch sizes & KV cache hit rates; I added a sensitivity table.

2) Safety/hallucinations: The examples on pages 6-8 appear to be prompt-sensitive and reproduced across 5 seeds in our harness for the open-llama-13b-q4 runs. For gptx-40b-finetune the failure rate was much lower (<1%), and redwood-instruct-7b had middling behavior. We'll attach a short eval manifest in the shared doc showing which prompts triggered hallucinations and the raw outputs. Long-term: we recommend model-specific prompt engineering + safety layer (post-process checks) for highest assurance.

3) Technical deep-dive: Thursday 11am PT works for us. Rishi and Dev will join and I can include our Runtime eng lead (Jonas Weber) for kernel/latency questions.

Next steps I’ll action this morning:
- Share the detailed eval manifest and a short runbook for the pilot (within the hour).
- Book the Deep-dive invite for Thu 11am PT and add a brief agenda.

If you want, we can pre-wire the pilot config (routes, canary %s, SLAs) so procurement has an estimate for the Reserved Dedicated cost.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Joe Turner <joe.turner@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme model shortlist & recommended next steps

Thanks team — just adding a couple of technical notes ahead of Thurs: 

- For the pilot config, we'll precompute KV cache retention tuned to your avg convo length; expected cache hit %s will materially reduce per-token cost for redwood-instruct-7b and gptx-40b-finetune. I added expected delta numbers in the spreadsheet.
- We'll propose a canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to your prompt set.
- Dev: can you confirm the preferred auth/token rotation approach for the Dedicated pool (KMS vs customer-managed HSM)? We'll prime the procurement estimate once we have that.

I'll take the lead on the runbook and the eval manifest Marissa mentioned. Booked the Thu 11am PT invite and added Jonas (runtime) + Mei (SRE) from our side.

Rishi
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
